correctness.rationale: A divisor formed from powers of the two distinct primes is coprime to an input exactly according to its two prime-divisibility indicators. The allowed divisor sets for the three restricted classes are, respectively, the unit alone, the unit and all positive powers of the second prime through its given exponent, and the unit and all positive powers of the first prime through its exponent. These sets overlap only at divisor 1. Partitioning all matchings by the class using divisor 1 yields the three disjoint falling-factorial terms; a T member forces 1 and two T members are impossible. End cases with B=0,C=0, saturation, negative x, and x=0 follow from exact zero-extension and gcd. A separate bitmask permanent implementation checked 7776 progressions and 846 complete occupancy profiles for small parameters. Finite verification does not substitute for the universal partition proof.

originality.rationale: The closest full text, Alekseyev arXiv:2610.37512v1 Theorem 1.1, decides whether an arithmetic-progression matching exists, not the exact number of matchings. The count is not implied by its separate prime capacities: for n=225 two arithmetic progressions each have three multiples of 3 and two of 5 but give 480 and 288 matchings. McNew–Pomerance studies existence/density; Sah–Sawhney gives interval-permutation asymptotics for a different bipartite graph. Targeted scholarly record and public searches found no evaluated two-prime-power divisor permanent. Priority remains uncertain with respect to general rook/permanent literature.
residual_risks: Earlier general rook-polynomial or permanent formulas for restricted bipartite graphs could specialize to the present expression without matching its number-theory terminology.
Unindexed older specialized enumeration literature may include an equivalent formula.
Independent mathematical and priority audits have not been performed.

value.rationale: Coprime matchability of divisor sets is an active natural arithmetic problem; the recent general theorem provides an existence criterion for progressions. The evaluated full matching count for the entire unbounded two-prime-power family is the first meaningful support level with overlapping constraints. The natural enumerative invariant cannot be reconstructed from the known one-prime existence data, as two progressions for n=225 have the same prime counts but 480 vs 288 matchings. The exact arbitrary-set Hall obstruction is additionally classified. No unsupported downstream theorem is asserted.
